knowledge_gaps: Sampled/full-catalog hit disagreement partly follows mechanically from candidate-set size: with identical exclusions and tie handling, sampled target rank cannot exceed full-catalog rank. The report needs a sampling-aware reference before interpreting disagreement as a model weakness.

Lexical retrieval does not specify whether its query is the target title or the observed prefix. Target-conditioned retrieval measures item confusability; prefix-conditioned retrieval measures history-related competition. These require separate interpretations.

Conflict filtering changes candidate counts and makes HR@10 easier. Sets with fewer than ten distractors yield automatic hits. Repeated targets already present in the prefix also require an explicit eligibility policy that retains the target consistently.

Reproduction requires concrete example and user limits, prefix selection, frequency-weight formulas, TF-IDF settings, fallback rules, score tensor shapes, user-level aggregation, runtime limits, and a generated-predictor parity procedure. The code-analyzer description also conflicts with the reported perturbation diagnostics; their implementation provenance is unresolved.

Training-prefix memorization limits conclusions. No measured link supports the potential rating of 7 or establishes that this audit should precede deployment verification and feedback grounding. Mean cosine near zero also cannot exclude low-rank representation collapse.

follow_up_queries.reason: Distinguish expected candidate-count effects from informative diagnostic failures and define fair filtered comparisons.
follow_up_queries.query: In recommendation evaluation, how can uniform sampling without replacement predict sampled HR@10 from a known full-catalog target rank using a hypergeometric distribution? How should candidate counts, ties, and removal of known-positive conflicts be controlled when comparing uniform, popularity-weighted, and lexical candidate sets?

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve what lexical competition measures and specify a reproducible audit without using lexical scores in prediction.
follow_up_queries.query: For a frozen NextItNet training-prefix diagnostic using only item titles and descriptions, how do target-conditioned TF-IDF hard-negative retrieval and history-prefix-conditioned retrieval differ in interpretation, false-negative bias, and shortcut risk? What query construction, tokenization, similarity, missing-text fallback, and repeated-item eligibility rules should be reported?

follow_up_queries.reason: Assess whether the audit provides actionable evidence beyond memorized training ranks within the fixed single-model benchmark.
follow_up_queries.query: What evidence supports using training-set candidate-distribution stress tests to guide sequential recommender improvements? For one NextItNet checkpoint per category, what bounded protocol combines user-clustered uncertainty, generated-predictor score parity, and a prespecified single-model intervention evaluated by unchanged validation HR@10, while limiting adaptive validation overfitting?
